DIJAN, CESO IV Regional Director, DILG-Regjon III Brgy, Maimpis, San Fernando Pampanga Dear Dir. Dijan: This pertains to the letter of OIC Provincial Director Honorio L. Castillo of DILG, Tarlac seeking our legal opinion/guidance regarding the demand of Avelino S. Tanjuakio, Jr. for the payment of his honorarium during his suspension. Per the letter of Maria Teresa P. Marquez, CLGOO, DILG Tarlac City, the Office of the Deputy Ombudsman for Luzon rendered a Decision on 26 November 2009 finding respondent Avelino S. Tanjuakio, Jr. (the then Sangguniang Barangay Member) guilty of misconduct and conduct grossly prejudicial to the best interest of the service and meting upon him the penalty of suspension from office for six (6) months without pay. The said Decision was implemented and respondent Tanjuakio, Jr. started to serve his suspension on 18 June 2010 until the end of his term of office on November 30, 2010, equivalent to five (5) months and twelve (12) days. Based also on the records you have forwarded to this office it appears that the Office of the Ombudsman issued an Order on 20 August 2010 granting the Motion for Reconsideration filed by the respondent and setting aside the decision dated 26 November 2009. Based on the said Ombudsman Order, Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr. is now claiming for his honorarium equivalent to five (5) months and twelve (12) days. Consequently, Punong Barangay Elena May S Vega of Barangay San Sebastian, Tarlac City sought the opinion of the Office of the Ombudsman regarding the demand of Mr. Avelino S. Tanjuakio, Jr. for the payment of his honorarium during his suspension.

In the letter-reply dated April 18, 2011 signed by Dir. Joaquin F. Salazar, Director EIO-A of the Office of the Deputy Ombudsman for Luzon, Punong Barangay Vega was advised to seek first the guidance of this Department before said Office will act on the demand letter of Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr. and wait for this Department's instruction considering that the query of Punong Barangay Vega involved the application of the provisions of the Local Government Code. In reply thereto, please be informed that the provisions of the Local Government Code particularly Sections 60-68 are applicable only to the administrative proceedings before the Sanggunians or the Office of the President. Since the Order setting aside the Ombudsman Decision dated 26 November 2009 and dimissing the case against respondent Tanjuakio, Jr. was issued by the Office of the Ombudsman, it is the Ombudsman Act or RA 6770 that will govern and not the Local Government Code. However, for academic purposes, may we invite your attention to the Supreme Court ruling in the case of EDGAR R. DEL CASTILLO VS. cliv11L SERVICE COMMISSION, PROFESSIONAL REGULATION COMMISSION AND/OR ASSOCIATION COMMISSIONER MARIANO A. MENDIETA OF THE PROFESSIONAL REGULATION COMMISSION [G.R. NO. 112513, August 21, "In so many cases, this 1997] wherein the Supreme Court provides that: Honorable Court had the occasion to rule as follows: It is already settled in this jurisdiction that a government official or employee is entitled to backwages not only if he is exonerated in the administrative case but also when the suspension is unjustified. [MIRANDA VS. COA, 200 SCRA 657] citing Abellena vs. City of Baguio, 19 SCRA 600 citing Reyes vs. Hernandez, 71 Phil. 297; Villamor vs. Lacson, G.R. L-15945, Nov. 28, 1964]. Such right [to backwages] is afforded only to those who have been illegally dismissed and were thus ordered reinstated or to those otherwise acquitted of the charge against them. [Isabelo T. Sabello vs. DECS, 180 SCRA 623]" Also, "when an official or employee was illegally dismissed and his reinstatement has later been ordered, for all legal purposes he is considered as not having been left his office, Therefore, he is entitled to all the rights and privileges that accrue to him by virtue of the office he held, (Tafiada vs Legaspi, 13 SCRA 566)." Applying the above-mentioned Supreme Court ruling to the case of Mr. Tanjuakio, it is our considered view that Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr. is entitled to his honorarium and any benefits accruing to him by virtue of the office he held during the time that he was serving his suspension for the following reasons, to wit; First, it was provided in the Ombudsman Order that the respondent (Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr.) had sufficiently rebutted the complainant's allegation, hence the case was dismissed. As such, there being no

complaint/case against Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr. because it was already dismissed, technically, Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr. is therefore exonerated. Second; the administrative case filed against Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr. was dismissed by the Office of the Ombudsman in its Order dated 20 August 2010 for the Motion for Reconsideration filed by Mr. Tanjuakio, Jr.,only after he was able to serve his suspension. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter, subject to the position to be taken by the Ombudsman. A . JES B. DO Director 111 Dir. HonoriöL.
